sections.html:
Ankeny is a suburb in north-central Polk County, just north of Des Moines. Interstate 35 runs along the east side and U.S. Route 69 goes through the center of town. When you describe a house to a buyer, name the nearest main road, because distance to I-35 or U.S. 69 is one of the first things people from the Des Moines area ask.

The city has grown fast, and it is now the fifth-most populous in Iowa.

Population more than doubled between 2000 and 2020, so many houses were built in that stretch. Their roofs, furnaces and water heaters are now at an age where replacement decisions come up, and that is often what pushes an owner to sell.

Most of the city lies in the Ankeny Community School District, the sixth-largest in Iowa, with nearly 12,000 students and 16 buildings. Parts of Ankeny are served by the Saydel and North Polk districts. The district line does not follow city limits, so confirm the district for your specific address using the district's own boundary tools before you describe the house to anyone.

Prairie Trail is a large planned development built on a former Iowa State University research plot. The city bought the land in June 2005 for $23.6 million and sold it to a developer in September 2005. The city agreed to invest up to $20 million in basic infrastructure, which gave the district its own streets, utilities and commercial space.

Homes in newer developments like this one often carry different covenants, association dues or special assessments than older houses near the center of town. Ask the title company to pull those records before you set a closing date.

Ankeny has hot summers and cold winters, with about 37 inches of precipitation and about 25 inches of snow in an average year. The record high is 106 degrees Fahrenheit and the record low is minus 34. A house here has to handle both extremes, so the furnace, the air conditioner, the roof and the sump pump all do real work.

If any of those are near the end of their life, a cash sale lets you sell without replacing them.

sections.h2: What to gather before you contact a buyer
sections.html:
A short stack of documents makes a sale faster, because the title company can start work the day you accept an offer.

  • The names exactly as they appear on the current deed, and a copy of the deed if you have one.
  • The latest property tax statement, so the closing agent can check for unpaid installments.
  • The mortgage lender's name and an approximate payoff, if there is a loan.
  • Any homeowner association contact, since newer subdivisions often have one.
  • A list of known problems with the roof, plumbing, electrical or foundation.

Polk County records the deed and keeps the tax records for the city, so your parcel is found under Polk County and not through a separate Ankeny office.

Every owner of record must agree to the sale and sign the deed. If an owner has died, the estate has to be opened or the title cleared another way before the house can transfer.

That step is usually the longest part of an inherited sale, and it does not change just because the buyer pays cash. What a cash buyer changes is everything after it: no lender review, no appraisal to schedule and no repair negotiation. Heirs who live in different places can sign separately, so nobody has to travel to Ankeny for the closing.

Tell us who the heirs are, whether a will exists and whether the estate has been opened. We will tell you what the title company is likely to ask for.

sections.h2: From first message to closing day
sections.html:
The order of events is the same for most Ankeny sales. First you send the address and a plain description of the house. We review it and write you an offer. You can accept it or turn it down, and nothing is owed either way. If you accept, a title company opens the file and checks who owns the property, whether a mortgage or other lien is attached, and whether tax installments are open.

While that title work happens, you keep your move plans flexible. Because no lender is involved, nobody needs to schedule an appraisal or wait for a loan committee. Once title is clear, the closing is set for a date that suits you. At the closing table you sign the deed and the statements the recorder requires. Any mortgage payoff and open property tax are paid from the sale price, and you receive the rest.

A financed buyer usually brings an appraisal, an inspection report and a list of repair requests. Each one is a place where a sale can stall or the price can drop. A cash purchase as-is leaves those out, so a house with an aging roof, an old furnace or a tired water heater is judged for what it is rather than what it needs.

It does not skip honesty. You still describe known problems accurately in the paperwork, and liens, back taxes and covenant questions from a newer subdivision still have to be cleared. Sorting those out early is what keeps the timeline short.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Ankeny
sections.html:
A cash sale is a direct purchase with no lender, so it can close on a date you choose once title work is done.

  • You send the address and describe the condition, including any repairs you have skipped.
  • We review the property and give you a written offer you can accept or decline.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence, as Iowa law requires.
  • Transfer tax applies to the sale price over $500 unless the deed states an exemption.
  • The deed is recorded with the Polk County Recorder.

If the house belongs to an estate or has more than one owner, every owner has to sign. Tell us early about co-owners, since that is the most common reason a closing date slips. A seller who is relocating for work, or who has a firm move date, can ask for a closing scheduled around it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Ankeny?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 67,887 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 77,833. Ankeny is the fifth-most populous city in Iowa.
Polk County. Ankeny sits in the north-central part of the county, just north of Des Moines.

faqs.q: What are the main roads through Ankeny?
faqs.a: Interstate 35 borders the east side of the city and U.S. Route 69 runs through the center.

faqs.q: What school district is Ankeny in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Ankeny Community School District. Parts are served by the Saydel and North Polk districts.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ankeny house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the home in its current condition, so you do not need to make repairs first. You still need to disclose known problems accurately.
